comments.text: Watching from Australia. It’s hard to watch this and totally comprehend just how many humans are actually living in conditions like this. Firstly, it brings home the fact of just how over populated some places in the world are and it’s truly horrific & absolutely heartbreaking 💔 Secondly, it reminds me of just how much the great divide of wealth has become in society. I am considered a low income worker here in Australia but to any of these people, I would surely be considered well off, if not rich. I only wish that the Big corporate companies and the super wealthy could see past their noses to aid those living in poverty, through no fault of their own. I know some do, but many don’t and never will. And of course, our Governments should do more. I invariably find it’s the people that can least afford it, that are the most charitable. I give what I can to several charitable organisations, as do many others …, but it’s never enough. We need to undertake a global treaty to address basic living conditions for all because at the end of the day, it’s not a privilege but a human right. 🥺

The Ghazipur garbage mountain is finally shrinking. Around 24 lakh metric tonnes of legacy waste have been processed and nearly 20 acres of land reclaimed. Biomining capacity is also being increased substantially.

A lot still remains to be done, especially since fresh waste continues to arrive, but the current target is to clear the remaining legacy waste by December 2027.

After decades of watching this mountain grow, seeing it finally shrink is genuine progress. Credit where it is due.
